description: City of Toronto publishes the register of properties listed or designated by City Council under Parts IV and V of the Ontario Heritage Act (an inventory begun in 1973 and described as about 10,000 properties, from landmark buildings to private homes), with a readme in the shapefile, and the companion Heritage Conservation Districts layer of areas protected by municipal by-law under Part V; a separate portal dataset (heritage-conservation-districts) carries the districts. Coverage: the City of Toronto; the register record was last modified on 2026-09-01 with quarterly refresh, and the districts record on 2026-06-24. Format and access: Shapefile, downloadable without registration from the City of Toronto Open Data portal; the portal also serves the metadata through a public API. Licence (read on the portal page on 2026-09-29): Open Government Licence - Toronto, as shown on the dataset page (the CKAN API licence field reads "License not specified"); cost: free. Caveats: the pages say the data are not intended for legal purposes without reference to council decisions and by-laws; the CKAN API licence field is empty although the page shows the Open Government Licence - Toronto; the shapefiles were not opened. Simulation uses: heritage-listed building layers for exposure and retrofit-constraint analysis in seismic, flood and energy-renovation models, and for district-level planning scenarios. Related catalogue records: Urban Form Toronto: built environment and walkability measures on a 100 m hexagon grid (data-toronto-urban-form-hex-measures); City of Toronto watermain breaks 1990 to 2016 (data-toronto-watermain-breaks); OpenStreetMap (data-openstreetmap).
